data.raw_text:
JUST IN: Mattheo Wovi Villanueva, a UPD College of Arts and Letters student, faces four charges following state forces’ violent crackdown against anti-corruption protesters in Mendiola last Sept. 21, his legal team says. 

Villanueva, who was merely serving as a security martial and paralegal for a media practitioner in the rally, is charged with alleged violation of BP 880, and the Revise Penal Code articles 146 (illegal assemblies), 151 (resistance and disobedience), 153 (tumults and other disturbances of public orders).

A video of the police manhandling and beating a defenseless Villanueva circulated online last Sunday.

The charges are yet to be filed as Villanueva still faces ongoing inquest.

ERRATUM: This post has been updated to clarify that Villanueva's charges are yet to be finalized, as he is still undergoing inquest proceedings. We apologize for the oversight.

China and Hong Kong have evacuated thousands of people as they prepare for the arrival of Super Typhoon Ragasa.

The storm, equivalent to a Category 5 hurricane, has already swept through the northern Philippines where at least 3 people have been killed. It has triggered severe flooding and landslides across the region.

Last week, protesters took to the streets of the Philippines capital Manila, furious about the alleged government mismanagement of money that was supposed to be used to protect the country from extreme weather.
